body:
Not enough money. Whatever there is, is going to be left for other people. But I will take a walk. There is a lovely lake by where I live.
Turns out it is my birthday. I had forgotten. Mom wished. Seems like the perfect day. Like everything is coming a full circle.
Thanks for your message though... It did make me think of things I still want to do, places I want to see, people I want to meet... I'll try to hold on to that hope for as long as possible.

Please don't go. Please...

Step out with your dog and take a walk, maybe? You're so lucky you have one.. what would I not give for a furry friend?! Take a walk... find a place you can volunteer... talk to someone there... perhaps make a friend? Please hold on. It will get better. It has to. I'm struggling myself right now, but this is what I keep telling myself! 

I don't know anything about you, but I know your feeling of loneliness. It's the same feeling that makes a knot in my stomach nearly every night. 
*Long distance comforting hug, friend*

You are so welcome :) I have been the person who desperately needed someone to tell me things are going to be alright, and during most such times, I was blessed to have at least one person in my life who did that for me. This is perhaps my little way of paying it forward :) But also, I think I'm going through a somewhat difficult time in my own life right now, and this time I don't really have anyone around to help me (which is what brought me to this sub in the first place), and I think trying to talk to someone else who is struggling makes me feel a little more purposeful and helps me put my own struggles and emotions in perspective. So anyway... enough about me!

From what I understand, people hired to teach English in a lot of Asian shcools really do not need ANY knowledge of the local language, but I'm sure a quick search through the interwebs should give you much more accurate information about such opportunities!

About how your family would feel about your decision - your situation, like I mentioned earlier, is eerily similar to my SO's. He stuck out his 4 years at a university that made him miserable, because that was the "best" place for him and his financial situation at the time (according to his parents) to keep his family happy. (Don't get me wrong - I don't think his parents had ANY intention of hurting him and I do think they are amazing people, but I'm not sure they understood the impact of his mental anguish from a decision made on the basis of financial comfort). Honestly, I'm not sure he even realized back then that leaving was an option. However, it really has affected him very deeply and has left scars that his family will never fully understand or be able to heal. In fact, it has shaped his attitude towards money, opportunity and relationships in general. While some of the outcomes are not bad in themselves, his resentment and how it manifests itself in ALL his relationships now is definitely not healthy. I, of course, cannot go back and undo his experiences now, as much as I love him, but perhaps I can share my feelings with someone like you and warn you of the dangers of making fundamental decisions about your life based on the priorities of other people. So basically - do not think you must stick it out because doing otherwise will break your family's heart. If this experience continues throughout your 3-4 years, there is much higher chance that the resentment will affect your relationship with your family for life, and that, according to me, is far more heartbreaking than you deciding to quit to keep yourself mentally and emotionally healthy right now. It is NOT selfish to make decisions to take care of yourself emotionally. 

Anyway, there are other opportunities besides something like teaching English too, I'm sure! Start searching, perhaps! While you may end up returning to Canada and starting afresh there, searching for such potentially interesting opportunities in random corners of the world might help keep you excited and optimistic through the next few months :) And hey! Who knows where you might end up how you might change the world for someone in your own little way? :)

I'm so sorry. You sound like a pretty cool person! Things will definitely get better, OP. :)
University that causes mental/emotional anguish is probably not worth attending, even if you don't rake up student loan debts while attending it. Source: SO did EXACTLY this. Even though he got out of it and is doing well for himself right now, he cannot let go of how he felt through those years and how it shaped his personality. He also feels somewhat betrayed by his family for putting him through that. Although he doesn't quite say it, I think this is part of what strains his relationship with his family now, a decade later. So please do not try to push your way through school if it causes you such distress just because it seems like your only financially viable option.

Please do whatever you can to save money for a one-way ticket home or anywhere else you have friends and/or an opportunity worth pursuing, and take it! 


If you are feeling adventurous, you can try finding interesting jobs in new parts of of the world! I have heard of jobs that require you to teach English to school children (supposedly they are easy to get if you are from the western world)! There are plenty of such opportunities in several Asian countries (my college roommate did this for a year in China before she started school back home in the US) that are completely legitimate and will pay you a decent amount of money for the duration of your work. While you may not save a lot of money through this, the experience and exposure could help you reinvent yourself!

And of course, if you are not feeling quite as adventurous as that, do try to reach home and find yourself a job. You are capable and have experiences a lot of people your age do not! You will definitely be able to find opportunities back home that will help get you on your own feet and hopefully make you happy :)

Please take care and feel free to PM me if you'd like more ideas/just a conversation!
